newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian politicians call for independent court.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian politicians call for independent court.

text.p: Several Cambodian politicians on Thursday called for the formation of an independent court, saying the current judiciary was unjustly controlled by co-Premier Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party.

Two members of parliament and opposition politician Sam Rainsy told reporters they feared imminent legal battles would be used as political tools against them unless an unbiased court with multi-party representation were convened.

"We don't believe the courts today are independent... the whole thing scares us," said Son Chhay, whose Buddhist Liberal Democratic Party recently has signed an alliance with co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party and Sam Rainsy's Khmer Nation Party.

The charges followed comments four days ago by Thomas Hammarberg, special representative of the U.N. Secretary-General for Human Rights in Cambodia, who described Cambodia's court system as "thoroughly corrupt" and in dire need of reform.

Son Chhay cited cases of Sam Rainsy -- who says he is being framed by Hun Sen for the murder of Hun Sen's brother-in-law last year -- and Prince Norodom Sirivudh, who plans to return in April after being exiled for allegedly plotting to kill Hun Sen.
Sam Rainsy said that without an independent court, the "state was set for a travesty of justice" against him at the hands of Hun Sen.
He has denied any role in the killing of Keov Samuth, Hun Sen's wife's brother who was gunned down last November.
On Monday, Hammarberg said Cambodia's human rights situation was poor, and cited cases of police and military beating suspects and a court system plagued by corruption.
